newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche says Breuer to succeed Kopper as CEO.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche says Breuer to succeed Kopper as CEO.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, said on Wednesday that management board member Rolf Breuer would succeed Hilmar Kopper as chief executive after the next annual general meeting on May 20.
"It is planned to propose Dr Cartellieri and Mr Kopper for election to the bank's supervisory board next spring," Deutsche said in a statement released after a meeting of its supervisory board.
The bank said Ellen Schneider-Lenne would leave the management board with effect from December 31 while Ulrich Cartellieri would leave the management board at the end of the next general meeting.

The statement said Kopper, Schneider-Lenne and Cartellieri would be leaving the management board at their own request. "At its meeting today, the supervisory board complied with those requests," the statement said.

The bank also said the supervisory board had appointed Josef Ackermann as full member of the management board with efect from today. Until the middle of the year Ackermann was president of the executive board of Credit Suisse.

At the end of the year Ackermann will first take over the staff division credit risks from Schneider-Lenne and then, in spring 1997, the market risks, treasury and economics division from Cartellieri, the statement said.
